title: Family income and hippocampal volume in childhood
abstract: In 231 children scanned in vivo, lower family income-to-needs was associated with smaller bilateral hippocampal volume (b=0.21, p<.01) from FreeSurfer segmentation.
note: clean include: SES + hippocampal volume + association

title: Parental education and amygdala volume in adolescents
abstract: Among 410 adolescents, parental education predicted amygdala volume measured with structural MRI. Higher education related to larger volume.
note: education is SES; amygdala volume; association reported

title: Neighborhood deprivation and hippocampal subfields
abstract: In 189 adults, area-level deprivation (IMD) correlated with CA1 and subiculum subfield volumes segmented from 3T MRI in vivo.

title: Subjective social status and limbic volumes
abstract: We related MacArthur ladder subjective social status to hippocampal and amygdala volume in 260 midlife adults. Lower status was associated with smaller hippocampal volume.

title: Income-to-needs and brain structure across development
abstract: In a cohort of 320 youth imaged in vivo, income-to-needs ratio was associated with hippocampal volume and cortical thickness. Volumes came from automated segmentation.

title: Poverty and amygdala volume in early childhood
abstract: Poverty-threshold status was related to amygdala volume in 96 preschoolers scanned in vivo with structural MRI. Poverty predicted larger amygdala volume.
note: poverty status SES; amygdala volume; association

title: Chronic stress reduces hippocampal volume in rats
abstract: Adult male rats exposed to chronic stress showed reduced hippocampal volume on ex vivo MRI compared with controls.

title: Maternal separation and amygdala growth in mice
abstract: Mouse pups undergoing maternal separation showed altered amygdala volume trajectories.

title: Socioeconomic status and the brain: a systematic review
abstract: This systematic review synthesizes evidence linking socioeconomic status to brain structure and function across the lifespan.

title: SES and subcortical volume: a meta-analysis
abstract: We meta-analyzed 28 studies of socioeconomic status and subcortical volumes, including hippocampus and amygdala.

title: Family income and cortical thickness in youth
abstract: In 300 youth, family income was associated with cortical thickness across frontal and temporal cortex. No subcortical volumes were analyzed.

title: Socioeconomic status and white matter microstructure
abstract: Diffusion MRI in 150 adults related socioeconomic status to fractional anisotropy in major tracts. No volumetric outcomes were reported.

title: Income and amygdala reactivity to threat
abstract: Using task fMRI in 120 adults, lower income predicted greater amygdala reactivity to threat faces. No structural volumes were measured.

title: Screen time and hippocampal volume, controlling for SES
abstract: We examined screen time and hippocampal volume in 180 children, adjusting for socioeconomic status as a covariate. The SES-volume relationship itself was not reported.

title: Hippocampal volume in a child raised in deprivation: a case report
abstract: We describe structural MRI findings in a single child raised in severe socioeconomic deprivation.

title: Pilot study of poverty and hippocampal volume
abstract: In this pilot of 12 adults, we related an income measure to hippocampal volume in vivo. Findings are preliminary.

title: Socioeconomic status and subcortical structures
abstract: In 240 adults, socioeconomic status was related to subcortical structure volumes in vivo. The specific structures are listed in the full text.

title: SES and the developing brain
abstract: Conference abstract. Preliminary findings on socioeconomic status and brain development will be presented. Sample and methods to follow.

title: Deprivation and brain volume in adolescence
abstract: We related deprivation to brain volume in adolescents. Regions of interest and sample size are described elsewhere.
note: outcome region and N not stated

title: Income and hippocampal volume, adjusted analyses
abstract: In 200 adults we studied cognition and hippocampal volume. Income was included in adjusted models. Whether income itself related to volume is not stated in the abstract.
